title: Gakoni Adventist College student strike and reported class refusal after a peer’s suspension/removal
location: Gakoni Adventist College, Gatsibo District, Eastern Province, Rwanda
organizer: Students at Gakoni Adventist College; no named organization is reported.
participants_original: KT Press reports that students struck and refused classes; MUHAZI YACU says all students protested. Neither report gives a simultaneous gathering count.
threshold_50_evidence: Not established. Neither opened report gives a protest headcount or a clear qualitative estimate at or above 50. A quoted account of a student meeting does not establish a public meeting of at least 50. The 16 arrests, enrollment of 372 (including 288 refugees), and photo caption of 15 students are not turnout counts.

title.summary: Both opened reports describe student protest activity at Gakoni Adventist College following the removal or suspension of a peer.

start_date.summary: KT Press dates the property-damaging strike to Sunday 7 February 2021.

end_date.summary: The reports describe class refusal on 8 February, closure on 9 February, and a 26 February reopening announcement, but none gives a physical end date for protest activity.

location.summary: The reports identify Gakoni Adventist College in Gatsibo/Eastern Province.

scope.summary: The reported actions concern students at one school; no broader coordinated geographic scope is established.

organizer.summary: Students are described as the participants; no named organization or formal organizer is identified.

demands.summary: A student quoted by MUHAZI YACU describes a condition to resume only after a peer was released and returned. The report does not identify whether the condition was directed to school management, local police or another competent Rwanda state authority, or government policy, and no listed demand category maps unambiguously to the school-level condition, so demands remains empty.

participants_original.summary: One report refers to students striking/refusing classes and the other says all students protested, but neither reports a simultaneous crowd count.

participants_min.summary: No defensible numeric minimum for attendance is reported; arrest, enrollment and caption numbers do not measure turnout.

participants_max.summary: No defensible numeric maximum for attendance is reported; enrollment and the photo caption are not turnout.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Neither source establishes a public assembly with 50 or more participants; school enrollment and arrests are not turnout.

protester_violence.summary: KT Press reports students stoning a police commander’s vehicle and property damage; MUHAZI YACU also reports property damage/resistance around a police vehicle. This is attributed reporting, not a claim about every student.

state_response.arrests.summary: The local reports state that 16 students were arrested; the later KT Press follow-up reports those students faced prosecution.

state_response.accommodation.summary: A ministerial reopening/management discussion is reported, but the sources do not establish that officials received or accepted the students’ stated demand; response remains unknown.

state_response.beatings.summary: The saved article read scopes do not establish event-specific beatings; the value remains unknown.

state_response.crowd_dispersal.summary: Police actions and arrests are reported, but a state attempt to disperse the protest is not established in the saved read scopes; the value remains unknown.

state_response.ignore.summary: The reports do not establish an explicit refusal to hear or avoid protesters; the value remains unknown.

state_response.killings.summary: No event-specific state killing is established in the saved read scopes; the value remains unknown.

state_response.shootings.summary: No event-specific state shooting is established in the saved read scopes; the value remains unknown.

eligibility.summary: Occurrence is reported, but public-meeting status, a 50-person threshold, and a demand to a competent Rwanda state authority (including local police) or government policy remain unresolved; this is pending evidence, not an inclusion decision.

notes: KT Press (9 February) reports the property-damaging strike on Sunday 7 February and class refusal Monday 8 February; MUHAZI YACU (10 February) reports the 9 February school closure and quotes an unnamed student describing a release-and-return condition. The 7 February strike and 8 February refusal are distinct reported actions/dates; whether they form one continuous physical protest is unresolved. Neither the student account nor the reports establish a public meeting of at least 50 or a demand directed to school management versus a competent Rwanda state authority (including local police) or government policy. Trigger accounts conflict: KT Press attributes the suspension to repeated dormitory departures to drink; MUHAZI YACU describes different alleged conduct and a COVID-rules briefing. Both cite Gatsibo Mayor Richard Gasana. The 16 arrests, 372 enrollment, 288 refugee enrollment and “15 students” photo caption are not turnout. S006 is a same-publisher/byline follow-up with a later ministerial reopening/prosecution response, not independent event corroboration. January RW202101-S006 is prior-unit-only and is not new February corroboration. No physical end date is assigned.
open_questions: Was the protest itself a public meeting, and did at least 50 people assemble at the same time?
Was the reported release-and-return condition directed to school management, local police or another competent state authority, or government policy?
What was the physical end date of the strike or subsequent refusal, if one can be established?
Which reported account of the peer’s suspension/removal trigger is accurate, if either?
Can an original school, student, official, or independent contemporary account establish turnout, organizer, demand recipient, and event boundaries?
Apart from the reported arrests, what event-specific state-response dimensions occurred?
